set.description: Combined Arms brings several generations of Command & Conquer into one standalone OpenRA game. Allies, Soviets, GDI, Nod and Scrin share the battlefield, giving your group plenty of reasons to disagree about which army deserves the next rematch. Pick a faction you know, then take time to learn what this version does differently.
set.whyWePickedIt: This is for the group whose favourite C&C games never quite line up. One friend wants Soviet hardware, another wants Nod, and somebody inevitably picks the aliens. We'd start with a relaxed match and leave room to experiment: the fun is discovering how those familiar armies fit together under a different set of rules.

faq.a: Use the standalone Combined Arms package. It is a separate client, so choose Combined Arms when getting your group ready.
faq.q: Do I need to install stock OpenRA first?

faq.a: The project publishes Windows packages, a macOS disk image and a Linux AppImage. These are separate platform downloads.
GitHub release notes cover faction balance, unit changes and fixes. Check those when returning after a break rather than assuming your old build order still works.
faq.q: Where can I find changes between releases?

expected.description:
Combined Arms mashes Tiberium, Red Alert, Dune, and later C&C factions into one competitive OpenRA client. It ships as its own Windows portable from Inq8/CAmod; you do not install stock OpenRA first.

PlayBound's default OpenRA edition stays the official portable. This edition is the CA winportable: CombinedArms-*-x64-winportable.zip from GitHub releases. ModDB remains the project news page. The Combined Arms row on the Mods tab is left in place for anyone who already installed it that way.
expected.whyWePickedIt: Every faction in one balanced game.

credits.name: Inq8 and the Combined Arms team

faq.a: No. The winportable zip is a self-contained client. Stock OpenRA is the other edition on this game.

set.whyWePickedIt: We'd choose this for the RTS player who watches the terrain as closely as the enemy army. Collapsible cliffs and weapons that reshape the ground make a map feel less settled, while ion storms add another thing to worry about. It's an appealing experiment for a curious group, provided everyone is happy playing a changing playtest.

faq.a: The project documents destructible cliffs and weapon-driven terrain deformation. An approach that looked secure can change, so keep watching the battlefield instead of relying on one defensive position.
Storms have warning, active and clearing phases, with lightning strikes during the storm. Pay attention to the warnings rather than treating the weather as decoration.
faq.q: What happens during an ion storm?

faq.a: The published build is a prerelease playtest. Expect changes and bugs, and use the same build as the rest of your group.
DoGyAUT develops Crystallized Nexus as a reimagining of Crystallized Doom, built on OpenRA. Credit belongs to the edition project and the upstream engine contributors.

expected.whyWePickedIt: New RTS content on a trusted engine.
